title: Occult and Psychedelic Horror
description: Focuses on the occult and/or psychedelic dimensions of horror films and popular culture. Critical, historical, and theoretical approaches to fear, disgust, the monster, the supernatural, delirium, esotericism, limit experiences, “good” and “bad trips.”
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Pakistani Cinema: Exploring the Nation through Cinema from 1947-Present
description: What do you think when you think of “Pakistan?” What feelings does it engender? What visions does it (re)create? What about “Pakistan” and “cinema?” This course examines the idea of a national culture and the cinema of Pakistan in terms of major periods, themes, formal parameters, and institutions in relation to both national and international cultural histories. In choosing Pakistan and its cinema history which correlates with a complex political history of constantly changing regimes as our locale, we will both problematize and work through the concept of a national cinema culture through a burgeoning subfield of film studies, Pakistani cinema.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Reviving Analog Media
description: Explores analog media nostalgia and revival through various theoretical perspectives. Well discuss a range of analog technologies, including vinyl records, boomboxes, and VHS, focusing on the cultural history of these objects and the context of their resurgence today.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Russian War Films, 1911Present
description: Examines the genre of war films in Russian and Soviet cinema from the pre-revolutionary era to the present. Together, we explore films on Russian military conflicts from World War I to the ongoing war in Ukraine. Following the evolution of a wide range of cinematic styles through the historic peripeteia of Russian imperialist, Soviet, and post-Soviet societies, we explore how movies have shaped the countrys popular historical narratives. In addition to viewing and discussing a feature-length film each week, we discuss short readings on the history of Russian cinema. Students also write weekly posts on the viewing assignments, which will go towards the creation of a collective zine.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Media Art and Activism: Reinventing Zoom
description: In this seminar students learn about the history of interactive video technology, examine and conduct research on various interactive video experiments, and work in groups to create new ways of using video chat platforms like Zoom for fictional, documentary, and/or interactive mediamaking. Each group collaborates on and produces a final media project together, which is then presented and archived online.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Screendance
description: This course asks students to consider dance-like rhythmic movement to be integral to its representation as screen media. In addition to written assignments, students are asked to produce a short video production drawing on the reading and weekly screenings.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Short Format Film
description: Seminar surveys several fascinating issues regarding the history, production, distribution, and exhibition of short films. We examine the distinctive story and aesthetic/formal strategies used in many of the landmark short films and filmmakers from throughout cinema history. The emphasis is on more recent shorts. We explore the recent explosion of attention to shorts and the expanded opportunities available to filmmakers to get their shorts seen at film festivals, on cable, and perhaps most significantly, on the Internet.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis:Adaptation Studies: Screening Shakespeare
description: This seminar investigates how to study screen adaptations, focusing on Shakespeare, arguably the most adapted author. Film and TV-focused topics covered include intertextuality, critical race theory (#ShakeRace), and queer theory. Screenings may include: Haider, Romeo + Juliet, Game of Thrones.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Soundtrack Media
description: Soundtrack Media examines how the theory and practice of the soundtrack may help us understand the techniques and effects of synchronization and cognition. Students write about featured screenings and texts; and in addition, record and create a series short soundtracks as part of a final creative project.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
